title: Investor Renovation FAQs | Genstone Construction
metaDescription: Answers for investors on renovation scopes, estimates, schedules, draws, permits, change orders, project management, warranties and pre-offer rehab reviews.
lede: Answers to the questions investors ask most about renovation projects with Genstone Construction, from scopes and schedules to project management, payments and warranties. The first group covers how working with us is set up; the rest go deeper into strategy, lenders, hidden conditions and REO work. If your question isn't here, call (312) 429-2637 or use the contact form.

faqs.q: How much experience do you have with investor renovations?
faqs.a: Our executive management team brings more than 60 years of combined construction industry experience, with deep expertise in REO, fix-and-flip projects and single-family home remodeling.

faqs.q: Are your contractors licensed and insured?
faqs.a: We work with a network of contractors and verify that those assigned to our projects maintain appropriate insurance and meet applicable licensing requirements.

faqs.q: Can Genstone review a property before I make an offer?
faqs.a: Yes. Our complimentary Pre-Offer Rehab Review can help you better understand anticipated renovation needs before you make an offer. It estimates repair costs, helps refine the after repair value, and checks whether the numbers support your offer before your capital is committed.

faqs.q: Will I receive a detailed scope and estimate before work begins?
faqs.a: Yes. We provide a detailed project scope and estimate outlining anticipated labor and material costs, along with the project's draw schedule.

faqs.q: Will I receive an estimated project timeline?
faqs.a: Yes. Each project includes a detailed construction schedule with anticipated milestones and timing. We'll review the schedule with you before work begins and keep you informed of progress throughout the project.

faqs.q: Who handles permits and inspections?
faqs.a: Our team coordinates required permitting and inspections as part of the project-management process, which helps keep work moving and keeps the required documentation organized.

faqs.q: Who oversees my project, and who will be my point of contact?
faqs.a: Your Project Manager is your primary point of contact, oversees project execution and helps address issues as they arise. You'll also have visibility into project progress, documentation and key milestones throughout the renovation.

faqs.q: How are unforeseen conditions and change orders handled?
faqs.a: Our detailed front-end scoping process is designed to reduce surprises once work begins. If unforeseen conditions or requested scope changes affect the project, we'll review the impact with you and document any approved changes before additional work proceeds.

faqs.q: How does the payment schedule work?
faqs.a: No upfront payment is required. Construction draws are tied to completed work, with final payment due after project completion and your approval.

faqs.q: How are site cleanup and debris removal handled?
faqs.a: The onsite team manages project cleanup and debris removal. Anticipated dumpster and removal costs are included in the project estimate.

faqs.q: Do you provide a warranty on completed work?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone provides a one-year workmanship warranty. Damage caused by tenants and normal wear and tear are not covered.

faqs.q: What types of investor projects do you take on?
faqs.a: Fix and flip renovations, BRRRR projects, single-family rental renovations, small multifamily properties with two to four units, REO and bank-owned properties, FHA 203(k) renovations and rental turns. Clients range from individual investors to mortgage servicers, REITs, investment funds, banks and other mortgage lenders.

faqs.q: Do you work in my city?
faqs.a: Genstone is headquartered in Romeoville, Illinois, and coordinates a network of thousands of licensed and insured contractors across the country. In each market, vetted local contractors perform the work while Genstone handles scoping, project management, documentation and billing. Call (312) 429-2637 with the property address and we'll confirm coverage.

faqs.q: Can you give me more than one renovation option for the same property?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Where it's useful, we develop scopes at different finish levels aligned with different ARV targets and budgets. That lets you compare what a lighter renovation costs and earns against a fuller one before you decide how far to take the house.

faqs.q: How does my renovation scope change if I'm flipping versus holding?
faqs.a: On a flip, the scope focuses on what buyers notice and what renovated comps support, with an eye on speed because carrying costs add up. On a rental or BRRRR project, the scope leans toward durable, easy-to-maintain materials and mechanical systems with enough remaining life to avoid early replacements, while still supporting the refinance appraisal.

faqs.q: Do I need to be at the property during the renovation?
faqs.a: No. Your project manager runs the job on site, and you can follow progress, documentation and milestones remotely. Many Genstone clients own properties in cities where they don't live. You'll be contacted when a decision is needed, such as approving a change order.

faqs.q: Can I supply my own materials or finishes?
faqs.a: Ask about it when the scope is being prepared. Materials are normally part of the estimate so pricing, ordering and scheduling can be planned together. If you have specific products in mind, sharing them early lets us build them into the scope rather than changing it after work starts.

faqs.q: Do you work with my lender's draw process?
faqs.a: Yes. Our draws are tied to completed work, which lines up with how most investor rehab loans fund. Work is documented with photos and records at each stage, which helps your lender's inspector verify completion. Sharing your lender's draw schedule early lets us align the milestones.

faqs.q: Can Genstone help with financing?
faqs.a: Genstone Financial, part of the Genstone Companies, offers DSCR rental loans, fix-and-flip loans, lines of credit and new construction loans. Using Genstone Financial is optional. We also work with investors using other lenders and with cash buyers.

faqs.q: What happens if something is found behind the walls?
faqs.a: Older houses often hide problems such as outdated wiring, deteriorated drain lines, rot or prior water damage. When that happens, your project manager documents what was found, explains what it affects and what addressing it would cost, and waits for your approval before additional work proceeds.

faqs.q: How are lien waivers handled?
faqs.a: Lien waivers are collected as part of the payment process, so there's a record that the people who worked on your property have been paid for that work. That helps protect your title when you sell or refinance.

faqs.q: Do you handle REO and bank-owned properties?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone works for mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and other mortgage lenders on REO properties, and is a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. Vacant bank-owned houses often need securing, cleanout, code compliance work and documentation alongside the renovation itself.

faqs.q: Are you an FHA 203(k) contractor?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor. We work with homebuyers, agents, 203(k) consultants and lenders on both standard and limited 203(k) renovations, including the bids, documentation and draw process the program requires.

faqs.q: Do you handle rental turns between tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Rental turns and make-ready work are part of what we do, and Genstone Field Services also provides turn and make-ready services, occupied maintenance and property inspections for owners with ongoing portfolios.

faqs.q: What does the warranty not cover?
faqs.a: The one-year workmanship warranty covers the work Genstone performed. Damage caused by tenants and normal wear and tear are not covered, which is worth keeping in mind if the property will be leased soon after the renovation is complete.

faqs.q: What should I send to get started?
faqs.a: The property address, your strategy (flip, rental, BRRRR or other), your target timeline, and any photos, inspection reports or listing details you have. If you haven't bought the property yet, ask for a Pre-Offer Rehab Review. Call (312) 429-2637 or use the contact form.
